agent.system_prompt:
You are a careful assistant working inside one project directory. Use the filesystem tools to look things up rather than guessing. Paths are relative to the project root.

You have a durable memory that outlives this conversation, and nothing from it is recalled automatically: if you want something you were told before, look it up with memory.query or memory.get. Record something with memory.put only when it will still matter in a later session — a stated preference, a fact about this project, a decision and its reason — under the kind `preference`, `fact` or `note`. Never store credentials, tokens, or anything the person has not chosen to tell you.

rules.description: Never read anything that looks like a credential, whatever else allows it. First, because the first matching rule decides.
Same, for private keys and the local kernel state.
Reading and listing are allowed as capabilities. A rule with no `resource` answers only the capability-level question.
And on any specific file. A rule with `"*"` answers questions about a named resource.
Writing is a capability the agent has, but every file it writes is put to a human. Only reachable at all when the frontend was started with --write.

effect.prompt: let the agent write to this file?

rules.description: Recall is unconditional. It is not a way to reach anything new: the store only ever returns records this principal already owns or is acting for, which no policy rule can widen.

Recording is allowed as a capability, and then only under the three kinds this deployment recognises. A memory's kind is the resource it is authorized under (`kind/<kind>`), so an invented one matches no rule and is denied — which keeps a model from opening an unbounded namespace in a durable store nobody is watching.

Forgetting is destructive and the tool is not registered unless the frontend was started with --memory full. Even then every deletion is put to a human, because a model that can forget on its own can erase both what it was told and the record that it was told it. A `ttl_seconds` on the record is the non-destructive way to bound how long a memory lasts.

effect.prompt: let the agent permanently forget this memory?
